description.narrative: Det föreslagna programmets övergripande mål att bidra till miljömässig hållbarhet, klimatmotståndskraft och inkluderande utveckling genom att leverera följande övergripande resultat: 1. Förbättrade naturresurser, biologisk mångfald och ekosystemtjänster. 2. Förbättrad hållbar livsmedels­ och näringstrygghet. 3. Förbättrad utveckling av inkluderande försörjningsmöjligheter. 4. Ökad klimatanpassning och utsläppsbegränsning. 5. Minskade konflikter om naturresurser genom jämställdhetsintegrerad freds- och konfliktlösning mellan olika befolkningsgrupper

To contribute to environmental sustainability, climate resilience and inclusive development in Ethiopia. The programme will aim to achieve the following five interlinked results; 1: Improved natural resources, biodiversity and ecosystem services. 2: Improved sustainable food and nutrition security. 3: Enhanced inclusive livelihood development. 4: Increased climate adaptation and mitigation. 5: Reduced resource­based conflicts through gender­sensitive inter­community peace and conflict resolution.

The overall objective of the programme is to contribute to environmental sustainability, climate resilience and inclusive development in Ethiopia. The goal will be achieved through five mutually reinforcing outcomes as follows: Outcome 1: Improved natural resources, biodiversity and ecosystem services. Outcome 2: Improved sustainable food and nutrition security. Outcome 3: Enhanced inclusive livelihood development. Outcome 4: Increased climate adaptation and mitigation. Outcome 5: Reduced resource-based conflicts through gender-sensitive inter-community peace and conflict resolution.

1. Overall
The 2024 results reporting was based on the revised and agreed-upon Log Frame dated 2nd January 2025. Compared to the baseline indicators (2023) and the corresponding annual targets (2024), results meet or surpass set targets.
In 2024, the NSSID project was implemented in 13 Woredas of three regional states, namely Oromia, Somali and Central Ethiopia.
The 2024 narrative report also documented systemic changes which the partner considers are taking hold. These are summarized as "Best Practices" in Section 5, p. 53-54. Taking the fact that the program is in its 2nd year of implementation, this effort is commendable.
On mobilizing partners (with clear incentives), the report provided examples in which local communities, local government, universities and local research institutions are collaborating. Section 9 of the report (p. 56) provides a short summary. In the case of communities and local government, evidence for "cost-sharing" was also documented (See Table 10, p. 57 of the narrative report).
2. Results by Outcome Areas
2.1 Outcome 1: Improved natural resources, biodiversity and ecosystem services
a) Reduction in Deforestation
- Forest area managed: 13 583 hectares since 2023.
- Deforestation rate: Reduced to 1.37%, achieving 96% of the annual target and 87% of the baseline.
- Impact: Improved ecosystem health; enhanced community livelihoods through sustainable resource use; increased resilience to climate change; and greater community engagement in conservation.
b) Enhanced Range-land Management
- Area rehabilitated: 258 hectares (102% of target).
- Beneficiaries: 395 people (307 men, 88 women).
- Impact: Improved vegetation and biodiversity; sustainable grazing practices; and strengthened local livelihoods and economic opportunities.
c) Strengthened Organizational Capacity
- Participatory Rangeland Management (PRM) cooperatives' capacity score: 83% (110% of target).
- Impact:Better resource management; stronger community engagement; and more effective implementation of sustainable practices.
d) Improved Watershed Management
- Area managed: 1 553 hectares (91% of target)
- Households participating: 1 177 (613 men, 564 women).
- Impact:Enhanced water quality and reduced soil erosion.
2.2 Outcome 2: Improved sustainable food and nutrition security
- The Average Household Dietary Diversity Score (HDDS) during the lean season in 2024 reached 7.2 out of a target of 7.88, which is 91% of the annual goal.
- An improving HDDS score indicates households are consuming a relatively high level of variety in their food intake during the lean season further attesting that efforts to improve dietary diversity were effective, contributing to better nutrition and food security among households during lean seasons.
2.3 Outcome 3: Enhanced inclusive livelihood development
a) Increased Revenue for participants: The 2024 Average Revenue was ETB 53 927 ETB (nominal); adjusted for inflation (at 17%), Real Revenue registered at ETB 46,091.45 ETB; compared to the 2024 target (Nominal= ETB 52 500 and Real = ETB 44,872), achievement is 103%. 1 128 individuals (509 female) participated benefiting from the diversified income interventions of the project.
b) Model Village Interventions: 88 farmer (8 female) participated in which they were equipped with essential practices to enhance agricultural productivity. These households adopted Farm Africas recommended practices, enhancing agricultural productivity and resilience.
c) Self-Employment Opportunities: The project facilitated 16 types of self-employment opportunities for 4 871 participants (3 121 females), generating 28 536 045 ETB (24 389 782 ETB, real) thereby improving livelihoods.
2.4. Outcome 4: Increased climate adaptation and mitigation
a) Adoption of Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA): Households adopting at least three CSA practices rose to 95% (2024 annual target is 92%), which is a 10% increase from the baseline. 1 433 farmers (500 female) participated and benefited from CSA interventions, indicating strong community engagement in sustainable agricultural practices.
b) Improved crop yields: The average crop yields for maize, wheat, teff, barley, ginger, pepper and haricot bean showed improvement from baseline exceeding the annual targets. 405 farmer households (106 female) participated increasing their crop yields. This improvement is attributed to adopting CSA practices, enhanced agricultural inputs, effective extension services, and better agronomic techniques.
c) Adoption of green energy technologies: Adoption of green energy technologies reached 84% (exceeding the 2024 annual target of 40%). 44 women adopted biogas, solar lighting, and other green energy technologies, enhancing energy sustainability within the community.
2.5 Outcome 5: Reduced resource-based conflicts through gender-sensitive inter-community peace and conflict resolution
a) Improved sense of safety: The percentage of individuals reporting an improved sense of safety increased to 15% (100% of the annual target). This is attributed to organized dialogue events, enhanced economic opportunities, and the active collaboration of community members and leaders.
b) Reduction in conflict incidents: Over the past 12 months, the number of reported conflict cases decreased from a baseline of 34 incidents to 27 incidents. 379 individuals (203 female) participated in forums aimed at raising awareness on conflict resolution relating to resource-based conflicts through collaborative efforts and education. Increased awareness and active participation in conflict resolution initiatives empower community members with the skills and knowledge to resolve disputes amicably, promoting a culture of dialogue and cooperation that enhances overall community resilience.
